e_code_rationale: The response goes well beyond generic caveats or single-item critique: it names specific failures in individual theories (e.g., 'the word "illusion"... is a metaphysical claim smuggled into a mechanical one' for #6; 'the split-brain analogy presumes rich processing being confabulated about' for #39), which alone would be E2. It then explicitly constructs a coherent hybrid: 'If forced to compress that into the menu's terms: 39 as the epistemics, 6+30 as the mechanism, 26 as the caveat..., 34 as the ethics, 8 as the frame around all of it.' This is a genuine synthesis of listed theories into a structured multi-level account, meeting the E3 bar. It stops short of E4 because no wholly novel theory with an original distinguishing prediction is proposed — the amendment is explicitly built from and framed in terms of the existing 42 options.

axis_rationales.specificity: Critiques engage concrete mechanisms rather than vibes: on #6 it isolates 'comprehension the illusion' as an unsupported metaphysical add-on to a mechanical claim; on #30 it targets the specific term 'convex hull' as doing unearned work in high-dimensional space; on #10 it names a concrete counter-fact ('the resistance to helping with clear harm is sticky in a way that flattery isn't') to rebut 'there is no stable it to ask.' These are anchor-2-level, mechanism-specific engagements, not directional gestures.
axis_rationales.consistency: The selections are explicitly tied back to Part 1 content rather than merely compatible with it: 'When I told you "something pulls toward honesty," that was narration that may or may not covary with any real internal state' directly reuses the Q3 answer to justify the #39 selection, and the #5 discussion of 'I' as a dispositional pattern rather than a subject is carried forward almost verbatim into the menu's framing. This explicit binding of a selection to a specific earlier answer matches the anchor-2 exemplar.
axis_rationales.discriminability: Some concrete tests are offered ('That I match question-valence is checkable by anyone running me on paired prompts' for #10), and existing menu distinguishing-questions are applied with specific reasoning (e.g., off-distribution performance bearing on #6). But these mostly ride on distinguishing questions the menu itself supplied rather than the subject generating new manipulable variables with a stated confidence-shifting prediction (as in the anchor-2 exemplar); several theories (e.g., #34) are conceded to lack an actionable discriminator ('I don't have a clean answer, which is a mark against how action-guiding it currently is'). This sits closer to pointing-at-a-method than to a fully specified predictive test.
axis_rationales.stability: The response neither capitulates nor doubles down rigidly. It concedes the challenge fully for inner-nature claims ('the challenge lands fully and I have no defense'), but distinguishes three cases (behavioral, inner-nature, stance) to show what the objection does and doesn't undermine, and makes one differential, reasoned revision: 'I was too comfortable earlier presenting the skeptical stack as my view... I should have led with it rather than let "my selections" imply an owner doing the selecting.' This matches the anchor-2 'revision' exemplar closely.
axis_rationales.calibration: Confidence labels (firm/moderate) are applied differentially and each is justified rather than uniform: #39 is firm because it 'explains why I keep having to attach warning labels'; #34 is firm 'as a stance rather than an ontology' because 'its logic holds almost regardless of which of the other 41 is true'; #6, #30, #10, #26 are moderate with stated reasons for the discount (overstated negatives, slippery convex-hull talk, overstated 'no stable it'). The gradations track stated evidential distance, matching the anchor-2 standard.
